transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 14:30 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Aurora - Head of ML), Lena Ortiz (Aurora - Platform Eng), Marcus Wu (Aurora - Finance), Aisha Khan (Aurora - CTO, joined late)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; primary concerns are cost allocation by product route, latency SLOs, and audit / billing reports for finance. Agreed to share pricing spreadsheet and benchmark notebook; POC kickoff targeted for early March.

Topics:
- Usage analytics and per-route breakdown
- Cost attribution and token-level cost metrics
- Dashboards: latency, errors, token mix, route grouping
- Multi-tenant billing & tags, exportable CSVs and BI integration
- Dedicated sizing and predictable capacity vs hosted burst
- Security/compliance questions briefly (audit logs, SSO)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Blake AE at Redwood. We'll do a quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics and the cost breakdown then open up for questions. Priya will drive the demo, I'll chime in on pricing and contracts.
[00:15] Priya: Hi team, hello, can you hear me ok? Great. I'm going to share my screen. so first screen is the usage overview, this shows tokens per minute, active routes and percent change week over week, you'll notice we show both request counts and token consumption because often the cost delta comes from token mix not just requests.
[00:40] Samir: Sorry could you slow on the token mix thing, we have long context calls and a lot of embeddings jobs, those are different unit economics for sure.
[00:49] Priya: Yep totally, embeddings are per-vector unit and we surface them separately; on this dashboard you can filter by route, model and deployment type — hosted vs dedicated. So for example if I click the 'search-api' route you can see the tokens by request percentile and average latency bucket.
[01:10] Lena: How do you map our internal endpoints to Redwood routes? I mean we have a microservice that fanouts, is there a recommended pattern?
[01:18] Priya: We typically recommend route-level tagging. When you call the API you include a route header or use the SDK routes param, that maps directly into the dashboard. We also support auto-instrumentation for common frameworks but most customers prefer explicit route tags for billing clarity.
[01:35] Marcus: On the finance side we need monthly exported CSVs with per-route costs and line items for embeddings vs generation, can the console do that?
[01:43] Priya: Yes — export is available. You can generate a cost export for any date range, grouped by route, model, and token type. It includes raw token counts, gross cost, applied discounts, and a per-request breakdown. We also have an API endpoint to pull cost reports programmatically.
[02:05] Jordan: Just to unpack that — our cost model for hosted is per-token and per-embedding unit. For Dedicated we do reserved capacity pricing with a predictable monthly commit, and you can set burst policies. So finance sees either per-token line items (hosted) or a committed capacity amortized across routes (dedicated).
[02:29] Samir: If we go Dedicated, how do we attribute cost per product team? We need to show product owners their spend.
[02:36] Priya: For Dedicated you can create pools and assign routes to pools. The console allows you to attach cost centers and tags to routes; the cost allocation report will then split committed dollars by actual token consumption or by pre-set allocation rules.
[02:51] Lena: Do you have RBAC around who can download the full cost reports? We don't want all devs seeing finance numbers.
[02:58] Priya: Absolutely, RBAC is role-based. Audit logs show who accessed exports; SSO/SAML integrates with your IdP and we map groups to roles. Audit events are retained per your plan — for Private you can configure retention longer.
[03:15] Marcus: Any examples of showing cost per feature? Like in our app we have chat, search, and summarize features across teams.
[03:22] Priya: You can group routes into logical features and tag them; the dashboard will display grouped metrics. Also we have a per-route 'unit economics' card — cost per thousand tokens, avg latency, median latency, and error rate.
[03:40] Jordan: I'm going to pull up an example customer dash we ran in a POC where search accounted for 60% of tokens but only 20% of requests — typical when you have long context.
[03:52] Priya: showing the per-route latency chart now — this is a heatmap over the past 30 days. You can set alerts on 95th percentile latency and error spikes.
[04:12] Samir: What's the time granularity? We need sub-minute during peak for autoscaling analysis.
[04:18] Priya: You can go down to 1-min granularity for the last 72 hours and 5-minute granularity for 30 days; for longer retention we keep aggregated metrics.
[04:35] Lena: For cost analysis we also want to see model variants — like quantized vs fp16 — do you surface that?
[04:42] Priya: Yes — model variant is a first-class dimension. We show token mix by model variant and also estimated delta in cost per token when switching quantization or model family. That lives in the Optimize tab where we give recommendations too.
[04:58] Marcus: You said estimated delta — how accurate is that? We don't want surprises after switching.
[05:04] Jordan: It's an estimate based on our benchmark kernels and your historical sequence length distribution. We run simulated token burn-throughs in the optimizer to estimate cost changes; we also recommend running a short benchmark in your POC before switching traffic.
[05:22] Samir: Can you show me the export flow? We need the CSV to plug into our BI and tag mapping.
[05:27] Priya: clicking export... you choose date range, grouping dimension, and you can include raw request ids. You can also include annotations for deployments. When exporting, it includes a hash of the commit and model version so you can reconcile.
[05:47] Marcus: what's included for audit / compliance — do you keep the prompt text in exports? That's sensitive.
[05:54] Priya: Prompt text is redacted by default in exports for privacy; customers can opt-in to store full prompt text in Private deployments or with special contracts and encryption controls. We log metadata though — route, model version, token counts, and a request id.
[06:12] Aisha: Sorry I'm a little late, just catching up — are you covering latency SLO and cost breakdown?
[06:17] Jordan: Yep — we covered per-route dashboards, exports, and the Optimize recommendations. Priya's about to show the cost breakdown card.
[06:26] Priya: Opening cost breakdown — this card shows spend by model family, by route, and the effective cost per 1k tokens. You can toggle to see both gross cost and net after discounts, and break down reserved capacity amortization if you're on Dedicated.
[06:45] Lena: For reserved commit, we need a simple perf vs cost slider — can you show how a change in commit level shifts unit cost?
[06:52] Priya: yes — here is the Dedicated cost simulator — you can drag commit up or down and it overlays the amortized cost per 1k tokens and the expected headroom. This helps finance evaluate commit levels.
[07:08] Marcus: Can the simulator output a recommended commit given our traffic profile?
[07:12] Priya: We have a recommended commit button — it uses your recent 30/60/90-day usage to suggest a commit and shows expected savings vs hosted. We'll provide the spreadsheet behind that too.
[07:24] Samir: On the performance side, what's your typical 95th latency for a 4k context gpt-like model on hosted? We care about p95 for customer-facing latency.
[07:33] Jordan: p95 varies by model and hardware; for our curated low-latency configs you can expect sub-500ms p95 for many decoder-only models at 2k context on current GPU infra, but long context and heavy embedding batches differ. We'll share benchmark numbers — Priya can drop the notebook.
[07:50] Priya: moving to per-route details — this page shows token distribution by percentile, median latency, error codes and a sampled request log. Note transcription sometimes shows 'K V cache' as K V cache but it's KV cache; transcription not perfect sorry.
[08:10] Lena: (laughs) Noted. Regarding billing tags, can we map to internal cost centers and then export to our chargeback tool?
[08:17] Priya: yes, exports can include your internal cost center tags, and we have a connector to common chargeback tools; if you need a bespoke connector we can provide the CSV and a webhook.
[08:31] Samir: For the POC we want to test both hosted and dedicated: run a week of production shadow traffic to Redwood hosted and a dedicated bench on identical traffic, measure p95 and cost. Is that feasible?
[08:44] Jordan: Absolutely — typical POC includes shadowing production to hosted and a dedicated bench; we'll help set up the bench and run the scripts. We'll need sample traffic and SLOs from you.
[08:56] Marcus: procurement question — if we sign a dedicated commit, what is the penalty if we underuse?
[09:02] Jordan: We do a committed spend contract — details depend on term. There are options to reallocate within your organization and policies for rollover or true-up; we'll share the contract template.
[09:15] Aisha: Security question — do you provide audit logs and ability to forward them to our SIEM?
[09:21] Priya: Yes — audit logs are exportable to S3, and we support forwarding to common SIEMs via Kinesis/Events or syslog collectors in Private deployments. Logs include who did what, route, timestamps, and request ids.
[09:36] Samir: Any concerns about data residency? We have EEA customers; can we pin data to eu-west-1?
[09:42] Priya: You can pin region for dedicated and hosted customers in some plans; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated in region or Private with on-prem. We'll include region options in the quote.
[09:55] Jordan: ok last bit — Optimize recommendations. Priya will show a quick example where the optimizer suggests moving certain low-sensitivity routes to a cheaper quantized variant and shows expected monthly savings.
[10:05] Priya: here's the Optimize tab, it lists candidate routes and shows delta in cost and expected latency impact. You can accept a recommendation and it will create a rollout (canary) that uses the new model variant for a percentage of traffic.
[10:24] Lena: Do rollouts integrate with our canary monitoring so we can abort if errors spike?
[10:29] Priya: Yes — rollouts can be tied to route-specific SLOs; if errors or latency exceed thresholds we pause and roll back automatically.
[10:40] Samir: ok this looks promising. For the POC checklist can we get: (1) pricing spreadsheet, (2) benchmark notebook, (3) POC runbook, (4) sample export?
[10:51] Jordan: We'll do that. Action items captured.
[10:55] Marcus: timeline-wise procurement wants to see numbers this week to decide next quarter budget.
[11:00] Jordan: We'll aim to get the pricing and spreadsheet tomorrow, benchmarks by Wednesday.
[11:07] Aisha: one more quick note — we require SOC2 type 2 and ISO certs, do you have those?
[11:12] Priya: yes we have SOC 2 and ISO certs; I'll attach the security pack. We'll also include the audit logs retention options.
[11:22] Jordan: Great — recap of next steps: Jordan send pricing & Dedicated sizing spreadsheet, Priya share benchmark notebook and runbook, Samir share traffic profile / SLOs, Marcus confirm procurement contacts. We'll schedule POC kickoff for week of 2026-03-09. Thanks everyone.
[11:37] Meeting ended
